documents.title: Responsible Use of AI at URI
documents.summary: URI's ITS page welcomes AI for teaching and research and sets four principles (transparency, accountability, fairness, privacy) plus data-security standards. It sets no classroom AI rule: educators communicate acceptable use and students follow each instructor's policy and attribute AI content.
documents.stance_why: The page "embraces artificial intelligence (AI) as a powerful tool for teaching, learning, research" but gives no default for coursework; it says educators should "clearly communicate acceptable AI use to students" and students "Follow instructors' AI policies", so the decision is handed to instructors.

units.why: Opening statement that URI "embraces artificial intelligence (AI) as a powerful tool for teaching, learning, research, and innovation" sets the institution-wide welcoming position, so actor all, general phase, informs. P56 chosen as it is the preamble of the framework; P87 fits less because it states a stance, not a list of benefits.
units.anchor: embraces artificial intelligence (AI) as a powerful tool for teaching, learning, research, and innovation
units.frag_start: The University of Rhode Island (URI) embraces

units.why: "ensuring AI is used securely, ethically, and responsibly to reflect our values of transparency, fairness, and accountability" states purpose and values for the page, so an institution-wide framework (P56); P116 is a close alternative but the sentence names the specific values.
units.anchor: ensuring AI is used securely, ethically, and responsibly to reflect our values

units.why: "Clearly disclose when AI tools are used to create content or make decisions" is a transparency principle requiring disclosure, addressed to all users; P24.
units.anchor: Clearly disclose when AI tools are used to create content or make decisions

units.why: "Validate the accuracy of AI outputs and take responsibility for their use" pairs verification with responsibility; P31 chosen because the first clause is the specific action, P29 fits the second clause only.
units.anchor: Validate the accuracy of AI outputs and take responsibility for their use
units.fit_note: Also says users take responsibility for the use of outputs (ownership, P29).

units.why: "Mitigate biases and ensure AI systems respect diversity and equity" is a fairness principle naming bias; P53.
units.anchor: Mitigate biases and ensure AI systems respect diversity and equity

units.why: "Protect sensitive and institutional data from misuse and unauthorized access" is a privacy and security principle; P50.
units.anchor: Protect sensitive and institutional data from misuse and unauthorized access

units.why: The page lists the Data Classification Schema as a key resource "relevant to AI practices", which is a pointer to further guidance (P115).
units.anchor: URI Data Classification Schema and Guidelines

units.why: The Guidelines for the Secure and Ethical Use of AI are listed as providing "comprehensive guidance on AI transparency, accountability, and compliance", a pointer to further guidance (P115).
units.anchor: Guidelines for the Secure and Ethical Use of Artificial Intelligence

units.why: "URI enforces the following standards" followed by "Follow URI's Data Classification Guidelines to avoid exposing restricted or sensitive information" is a data-protection rule; P50.
units.anchor: to avoid exposing restricted or sensitive information

units.why: "Ensure all AI tools comply with Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) and the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA)" requires accessible AI tools; P97.
units.anchor: Ensure all AI tools comply with Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG)

units.why: "Avoid inputting private or restricted data, such as Personally Identifiable Information (PII) or patient records, into public AI tools like ChatGPT" bars certain inputs; P50 rather than P20/P49, which concern assignment specs and course materials.
units.anchor: Avoid inputting private or restricted data

units.why: "Be cautious when using AI platforms, as data entered may be transmitted to third-party servers" warns that tools handle prompts; P50.
units.anchor: data entered may be transmitted to third-party servers

units.why: "Where possible, disable history and logging features to prevent information from being stored or used for AI training without consent" is a privacy-protecting practice; P50.
units.anchor: disable history and logging features

units.why: "Respect copyrights and avoid using confidential data in AI systems without appropriate protections in place" covers copyright and IP; P52 chosen for the copyright clause, while the confidential-data clause is partly P50.
units.anchor: Respect copyrights and avoid using confidential data in AI systems
units.fit_note: Also bars confidential data in AI systems without protections (privacy).

units.why: "Attend sessions on responsible AI use tailored for faculty, staff, and students" is a training offer for students and staff; P70.
units.anchor: Attend sessions on responsible AI use tailored for faculty, staff, and students

units.why: "Access documents and guidelines like the AI Use Guidelines to deepen understanding" points to training materials; P70 over P115 because the purpose is learning.
units.anchor: Access documents and guidelines like the

units.why: "Learn how to make AI tools and outputs more inclusive through URI's accessibility programs" directs users to accessibility training; P97.
units.anchor: Learn how to make AI tools and outputs more inclusive

units.why: "Before using any AI platform, take the time to understand how it works, what data it collects" asks users to assess a tool before use; P117.
units.anchor: take the time to understand how it works, what data it collects

units.why: Educators are told to "clearly communicate acceptable AI use to students"; this makes educators state expectations, so P09 (AI statement), instructors, course-start.
units.anchor: clearly communicate acceptable AI use to students
units.frag_end: AI was used to create course materials
units.fit_note: Does not mention the syllabus; says communicate acceptable use to students.

units.why: "Incorporate URI's guidelines into course design" tells educators to build the university guidelines into course design; no type covers aligning course design with university guidelines, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Incorporate URI
units.uncovered_note: Educators should build the university AI guidelines into their course design.

units.why: "disclose when AI was used to create course materials" is instructor disclosure of AI-made materials; P48 fits.
units.anchor: disclose when AI was used to create course materials
units.fit_note: Disclosure is stated; review of materials is not mentioned.

units.why: "Follow instructors' AI policies" makes each instructor's policy binding on students, a duty to follow course rules; P78.
units.anchor: Follow instructors
units.policy: Students follow their instructors' AI policies.

units.why: "properly attribute AI-generated content" requires students to attribute AI output; P24.
units.anchor: properly attribute AI-generated content

units.why: "avoid using AI in ways that breach URI's Student Code of Conduct" ties AI misuse to existing conduct rules; P77 rather than P36 because it does not classify misuse as misconduct or name a process.
units.anchor: avoid using AI in ways that breach

units.why: "Consult with your department and comply with regulations when using AI tools in research" sets research AI rules and defers to department and regulations; P62.
units.anchor: Consult with your department and comply with regulations when using AI tools in research

units.why: The page closes by naming a contact for "more information about URI's AI practices", a pointer to further help; P115, though it names a contact person, not a policy owner (P80).
units.anchor: karen_lokey@uri.edu
units.fit_note: Names a contact person for information, not an owner of the policy.

notes: Only the ITS page was included. The Graduate School news post was screened out.
